THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY,
ALOK ARADHE J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
JUDGMENT

This appeal under Section 47A of the Guardian and Wards Act, 1890 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act' for short) has been filed against judgment dated 27.01.2015 by which petition filed by the respondents i.e., maternal grand parents of the child viz., Jeevan alias Arjun, under Section 25 of the Act has been allowed and they were appointed as guardians of the minor child viz., Jeevan alias Arjun.
The appellant Nos.1 and 3 viz., the father and the paternal grand mother of the child were directed to hand over the custody of the child.
In order to appreciate the appellant's grievance, few facts need mention, which are stated infra.
2. The appellant No.1 and daughter of respondents viz., late Smt.Leeladevi got married on 21.11.2011.
A son viz., Jeevan alias Arjun was born to them on 08.11.2013.
Smt.Leeladevi committed suicide in the night intervening 07 & 08.08.2014.

On the basis of the complaint made by the respondents, First Inforamtion Report was registered against appellant No.1 for offences under Section 302 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code, Section 498A, 304B of IPC as well as under Section 3, 4 and 6 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
3. The respondents viz., the in-laws of the appellant No.1 filed a petition under Section 25 of the Act.
It was averred that appellant No.1 is residing at Kanivehally Village and they are neither any educational nor medical facilities available in the said village.
It was further pleaded that their grand child is suffering from deficiency of calcium and there is nobody to look after him.

Accordingly, the Rudreshachar vs Thipperudrachar on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109080695/
2 respondents No.1 and 2 sought their appointment as guardian in respect of their grand child viz.,
Jeevan alias Arjun.

sentences.text: The appellants filed their objections in which inter alia it was stated that respondents have made a false complaint against appellant No.1.
It was further pleaded that even after the birth of the child, the respondents did not visit to see him.
It was further pleaded that the appellant No.1 resides with his mother viz., appellant No.3 and they would take care of the child.
4. The family court on the basis of the pleadings of the parties, framed issues.
The respondent No.1 examined himself as PW1 and exhibited 8 documents viz., Ex.P1 to Ex.P8.
The appellant No.1 examined himself as RW1 and got exhibited 24 documents viz., Ex.R1 to Ex.R24.
The family court vide judgment dated 27.01.2015 inter alia held that the appellants No.1 and 3 reside in a remote village where neither the educational facility nor medical facility is available.

It is further held that a criminal case is pending against appellant No.1 and there is nobody to take care of the child viz.,
Jeevan alias Arjun.

The family court therefore, vide judgment dated 27.01.2015 appointed respondents as guardian of the minor ward Jeevan alias Arjun and directed the appellant No.1 to hand over the custody of the minor ward to respondents.
Being aggrieved, the appellants have filed this appeal.
5. Learned counsel for the appellants submitted that the appellant is an Engineer and is employed in Jindal Factory.
It is further submitted that the child is in the custody of the father viz., appellant No.1 and is aged about 9 years.
It is further submitted that the child is a student of III Standard.

It is also pointed out that the appellant No.1 has been acquitted on 05.10.2019 in the criminal case,
which was filed against him.
It is also urged that the appellants No.1 and 3 are taking proper care of the child.
6. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondents have supported the judgment passed by the family court.
It is further submitted that in case, the appeal is allowed, the respondents be granted the visitation rights.
7. We have considered the submissions made on both sides and have perused the record.
The appellant No.1 being the father of the child viz., Jeevan alias Arjun is his natural guardian.

However,
paramount consideration has to be given to the welfare of the minor.
The appellant No.1 admittedly is an Engineer and is employed in Jindal factory in Thorangal.
The appellant No.1 resides with his mother viz., appellant No.3.
The son of the appellant No.1 is aged about 9 years and is a student of III standard.
On account of any interim order passed by this court on 18.02.2015, the child remains in the custody of the appellant.
The appellant No.1 and his mother are taking care of the child.
It is not the case of respondents that the appellant No.1 is financially incapacitated to take care of his son.

8. It is also relevant to mention here that a criminal case was lodged against appellant No.1 for offences under Section 302 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code, Section 498A, 304B of IPC as well as under Section 3, 4 and 6 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, in which the appellant No.1 vide judgment dated 05.10.2019 has been acquitted.

Therefore, for the aforementioned reasons, taking into account the fact that the appellant No.1 has been taking care of his son and the natural guardian of the ward and in the interest of the welfare of the child, we set aside the judgment dated Rudreshachar vs Thipperudrachar on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109080695/
3 27.01.2015.
The appellant No.1 who is the natural guardian of the ward viz., Jeevan alias Arjun is appointed as his guardian.
The respondent shall be at liberty to visit the ward Jeevan alias Arjun on last Sunday of every month.
In the result, the appeal is allowed.
